items.stem: Which statement about organ systems in a living organism is correct?

options.text: Organ systems are made of one organ with one function.
Organ systems are made of cells grouped together.
Organ systems are made of one tissue with a function.
Organ systems are made of organs that work together.

items.why: Correct: organs are organised into organ systems, which work together to form organisms.

items.stem: A structure in an organism is made up of several different tissues that work together to carry out a specific function. Which level of organisation is this structure?

options.text: a tissue, a group of similar cells
an organ system, a group of organs
an organ, an aggregation of tissues
an organism, a group of organ systems

items.why: Correct: organs are aggregations of tissues performing specific functions, which is exactly what the structure described is.

items.stem: Enzymes are involved in metabolism. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Enzymes catalyse the reactions of metabolism in cells.
Enzymes give the reactions the energy that they need.
Enzymes are used up in the reactions that they speed up.
Enzymes catalyse only reactions that break down food.

items.why: Metabolism is the sum of all the reactions in a cell or the body, and each of those reactions is catalysed by an enzyme.

items.stem: Which statement about digestive enzymes is correct?

options.text: Bile is the enzyme that breaks down fat droplets.
One enzyme is able to digest every type of food.
Protease is made in the stomach and pancreas.
Amylase is made only in the wall of the stomach.

items.why: Protease is produced in the stomach, the pancreas and the small intestine, and it breaks down proteins to amino acids.

items.stem: What does lipase break lipids down into?

options.text: Glucose and fatty acids
Glycerol and fatty acids
Amino acids and simple sugars
Small droplets of lipid

items.why: Lipases break down lipids (fats) to glycerol and fatty acids, which are small soluble molecules that can be absorbed.

items.stem: What happens to the products of digestion after they are absorbed?

options.text: Every product is turned into glucose and stored.
They are all used in respiration to give energy.
They build new carbohydrates, lipids and proteins.
They join back to form the first food molecules.

items.why: The products of digestion are used to build new carbohydrates, lipids and proteins, and some glucose is used in respiration.

items.stem: Enzymes catalyse specific reactions. What causes this specificity?

options.text: The temperature at which the enzyme works.
The shape of the enzyme's active site.
The amount of the enzyme that is used.
The pH at which the enzyme is stored.

items.why: Enzymes catalyse specific reactions in living organisms due to the shape of their active site, which only one substrate fits.

items.stem: Which statement describes the lock and key theory of enzyme action?

options.text: The enzyme fits into every kind of substrate.
The enzyme is used up by its own substrate.
The enzyme changes shape to fit any substrate.
The substrate fits the enzyme's active site.

items.why: In the lock and key theory, used as a simplified model of enzyme action, the substrate is the key that fits the active site of the enzyme.

items.stem: An enzyme-controlled reaction is fastest at 40 degrees Celsius. What happens at 60 degrees Celsius?

options.text: The rate falls because the enzyme has been killed.
The rate falls because the enzyme is used up.
The rate rises because the enzyme works faster.
The rate falls because the active site changes shape.

items.why: Above the optimum temperature the shape of the active site changes, so the substrate no longer fits and the rate falls.

items.stem: Protease in the stomach works fastest at pH 2. What happens to its activity at pH 8?

options.text: It falls, as the active site changes shape.
It rises, as enzymes work best at about pH 7.
It falls, as the enzyme is killed by alkali.
It falls, as the enzyme has been used up.

items.why: Away from its optimum pH the shape of the active site changes, so the substrate no longer fits and activity falls.

items.stem: Amylase broke down 20 mg of starch in 5 minutes. What was the mean rate of reaction?

options.text: 4 mg per minute
0.25 mg per minute
20 mg per minute
100 mg per minute

items.why: The mean rate is the amount changed divided by the time taken: 20 mg divided by 5 minutes.

items.stem: Why does bile increase the rate of fat breakdown by lipase?

options.text: It digests the fat into fatty acids and glycerol.
It gives the lipase the energy that it needs.
It emulsifies fat, so surface area increases.
It makes the small intestine neutral at pH 7.

items.why: Bile emulsifies fat to form small droplets which increases the surface area, and the alkaline conditions and large surface area increase the rate of breakdown by lipase.

items.stem: Which statement about the double circulatory system is correct?

options.text: Blood passes through the heart once each circuit.
Arteries carry blood with oxygen to the lungs.
The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs.
The left ventricle pumps blood to the lungs.

items.why: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs where gas exchange takes place, while the left ventricle pumps blood around the rest of the body.

items.stem: Which feature of the alveoli increases the rate of gaseous exchange?

options.text: A wide tube that carries air down to the lungs.
A thick outer wall that resists air pressure.
A supply of plasma that takes up the oxygen.
A large surface area and a good blood supply.

items.why: The alveoli are adapted for gaseous exchange by a large surface area and the capillary network that surrounds them.

items.stem: Which pairing of a blood vessel with its structure is correct?

options.text: Artery: thick wall resists the high pressure.
Vein: thick muscular wall resists high pressure.
Capillary: thick wall resists the blood pressure.
Artery: valves stop blood flowing backwards.

items.why: An artery carries blood away from the heart at high pressure, so its wall is thick, with muscle and elastic fibres.

items.stem: A heart pumps 300 cm3 of blood in 4 seconds. What is the rate of blood flow?

options.text: 1200 cm3 per second
75 cm3 per second
300 cm3 per second
0.01 cm3 per second

items.why: Rate of blood flow is the volume divided by the time taken: 300 cm3 divided by 4 seconds.

items.stem: A photograph shows the cells in a sample of blood. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Platelets move around the blood and destroy pathogens.
Plasma is the liquid that carries oxygen to the cells.
Red blood cells have a nucleus that controls oxygen use.
Red blood cells have no nucleus, so they carry more oxygen.

items.why: A red blood cell is adapted to its function of carrying oxygen: it has no nucleus, leaving more room for haemoglobin.

items.stem: Which statement about the treatment of coronary heart disease is correct?

options.text: Statins are used to widen the blocked coronary arteries.
Stents are used to keep the coronary arteries open.
Stents are used to lower the level of blood cholesterol.
Artificial hearts are used to cure the heart disease.

items.why: In coronary heart disease fatty material narrows the coronary arteries, and stents are used to keep them open.

items.stem: A person has a heart valve that has developed a leak. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Blood flows backwards through the leaking valve.
The volume of blood pumped stays the same.
Only a heart transplant can treat the problem.
An artificial heart gives a permanent cure.

items.why: A faulty valve that leaks lets blood flow backwards, so less blood is pumped forward to the body.

items.stem: Which statement best describes health?

options.text: The state of being free of catching diseases.
The state of having no risk factors present.
The state of both physical and mental well-being.
The state of the body when disease is absent.

items.why: Health is the state of physical and mental well-being, so it is more than the absence of disease.

items.stem: Which statement about the interaction of different types of disease is correct?

options.text: Communicable disease has no effect on other illness.
Mental illness is not affected by physical illness.
Cancers are triggered by lifestyle, not by viruses.
An immune reaction to a pathogen can trigger allergies.

items.why: Different types of disease may interact: immune reactions initially caused by a pathogen can trigger allergies such as skin rashes and asthma.

items.stem: What is happening to the cells in a tumour?

options.text: Changes in cells lead to uncontrolled growth.
The cells in the tissue die and are not replaced.
Benign cells travel around in the bloodstream.
Lifestyle damages the membrane around the cell.

items.why: Cancer is the result of changes in cells that lead to uncontrolled growth and division.

items.stem: How do malignant tumour cells differ from benign tumour cells?

options.text: They stay inside a membrane in one part of the body.
They invade tissues and form secondary tumours.
They are caused by lifestyle rather than by genes.
They divide more slowly than normal healthy cells.

items.why: Malignant tumour cells are cancers: they invade neighbouring tissues and spread in the blood to different parts of the body, where they form secondary tumours.

items.stem: Why might an artificial heart be used for a patient with heart failure?

options.text: It keeps a patient alive while awaiting a donor.
It replaces a faulty valve inside the patient.
It cures the heart failure without any further care.
It lowers the level of cholesterol in the blood.

items.why: Artificial hearts are occasionally used to keep patients alive whilst waiting for a heart transplant, or to allow the heart to rest as an aid to recovery.

items.stem: A scatter diagram shows a correlation between hours of exercise and heart health. What can be concluded?

options.text: Exercise has been proved to cause good heart health.
People who exercise avoid getting heart disease.
The variables are linked, but no cause is proven.
The sample size does not matter for this result.

items.why: A scatter diagram can be used to identify a correlation between two variables, but a causal mechanism has been proven for some risk factors and not for others.

items.stem: A scientist studies whether a substance is a risk factor using data from 20 people. Why is this a problem?

options.text: A risk factor affects each person in the sample.
The sample size has no effect on the result.
A correlation in the data would prove a cause.
The sample is too small to be representative.

items.why: The principles of sampling applied to epidemiological data require a sample large enough to represent the population before conclusions are drawn.

items.stem: Smoking is described as a risk factor for lung cancer. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A correlation in data proves that it is a cause.
It is a factor linked to an increased rate of disease.
It is the one risk factor for this type of cancer.
It leads to the disease in each person who smokes.

items.why: Risk factors are linked to an increased rate of a disease, and smoking is a lifestyle risk factor for lung disease and lung cancer.

items.stem: What does xylem tissue transport, and in which direction?

options.text: Dissolved sugars, from the leaves to all parts
Water and mineral ions, from the roots to leaves
Cell sap, from each living cell to the next one
Mineral ions, drawn into the roots by osmosis

items.why: Xylem tissue transports water and mineral ions from the roots to the stems and leaves, carrying the water in the transpiration stream.

items.stem: How does a root hair cell take up water and mineral ions from the soil?

options.text: Water enters by osmosis and ions by active transport
Water and mineral ions both enter the cell by osmosis
Water enters by osmosis and sugars by translocation
Water enters through pores in the cells' end walls

items.why: Root hair cells are adapted for the efficient uptake of water by osmosis, and mineral ions by active transport.

items.stem: Which statement describes translocation?

options.text: Water and mineral ions move up to the leaves
Dissolved sugars move to the rest of the plant
Cell sap moves through tubes stiffened by lignin
Water and mineral ions enter cells by osmosis

items.why: Translocation is the movement of food molecules through phloem tissue, carrying dissolved sugars from the leaves to the rest of the plant for immediate use or storage.

items.stem: What is the role of the guard cells that surround each stoma?

options.text: They control gas exchange and water loss from the leaf
They are the pores through which gases pass in or out
They open more widely when the surrounding air is humid
They hold the air spaces in which photosynthesis occurs

items.why: The role of stomata and guard cells is to control gas exchange and water loss, the guard cells opening and closing each pore.

items.stem: Which statement describes the process of transpiration?

options.text: Sugars dissolve in cells and move down through the xylem
Water passes out through the guard cells acting as pores
Water vapour moves back into the leaf from the humid air
Water evaporates from cells and diffuses out of stomata

items.why: In transpiration water evaporates from the cells inside the leaf and the water vapour diffuses out through the stomata, and the water lost is replaced by the transpiration stream in the xylem.

items.stem: A potted plant is moved from a cool, shaded room with still, humid air into a warm, brightly lit room with moving, dry air. What happens to its rate of transpiration?

options.text: It decreases, as the drier air holds less water vapour
It decreases, as the moving air cools the leaf surface
It stays the same, as the same volume of water is lost
It increases, as water evaporates and diffuses faster

items.why: Higher temperature, higher light intensity, greater air movement and lower humidity each increase the rate of transpiration: the stomata open in the light and water vapour diffuses out of them more quickly.

items.stem: How is the structure of palisade mesophyll related to its function in a leaf?

options.text: Its cells are spread apart to let gases move around
Its cells are hollow tubes made stronger by lignin
Its cells contain many chloroplasts that absorb light
Its cells are one tissue that forms the whole leaf

items.why: Palisade mesophyll cells are packed with chloroplasts near the upper surface of the leaf, so the tissue is structured to absorb light for photosynthesis.

items.stem: A student measured the water lost by three identical shoots. Shoot A lost 1.2 cm3 in 60 minutes in still air at 20 degrees C. Shoot B lost 2.4 cm3 in 60 minutes in moving air at 20 degrees C. Shoot C lost 2.0 cm3 in 40 minutes in still air at 30 degrees C. Which conclusion do the results support?

options.text: The highest rate of water loss was in moving air at 20 C
The lowest rate of water loss was in moving air at 20 C
The highest rate of water loss was in still air at 30 C
Still air at 20 C gave the highest rate of water loss

items.why: Rate of transpiration is volume divided by time: shoot C lost 2.0 cm3 in 40 minutes, which is 0.05 cm3 per minute, higher than shoot B at 0.04 and shoot A at 0.02.
